patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with diabetes, hypertension, permanent AF on warfarin, prior stroke and PAD who joins in 2019. An exam-found AAA is repaired by EVAR in 2022 and complicated by cholesterol embolism; inclusion body myositis, distal esophageal adenocarcinoma, high-grade T1 bladder cancer and Waldenström macroglobulinemia follow, each treated, with an E. coli UTI in early 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT - establishing care

65M, retired construction foreman (ran crews for a commercial builder, mostly steel and concrete), here to take over primary care from his old office. Brought a bag of bottles. Old records requested, not here yet, so history is mostly from him and the bottles.

He has had sugar for about ten years, pressure longer than that. Has had AF for years and has been on warfarin the whole time; INRs were done at an outside lab with phone calls from the old office and he says nobody ever called back. Had a mild stroke in 2017, a few days in the hospital, fully recovered with no lingering problems. That's what made him quit smoking. Told he has blockages in the leg arteries a year or two ago, no claudication he can point to. Reflux controlled on omeprazole. Sees an outside cardiologist once a year for the AF.

Meds (verified with bottles):
- metformin 1000 mg BID
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- HCTZ 12.5 mg daily
- metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily
- warfarin 5 mg daily, adjusted per INR
- aspirin 81 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
- omeprazole 20 mg daily

Allergies: NKDA

Family: father died at 72 of a ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm. Mother had type 2 diabetes and macular degeneration. Paternal uncle had Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia. Brother with high blood pressure.

Social: married, lives in Florence. Smoked about 40 pack-years, quit 2017. Glass of red wine with dinner most nights, no more than that. Walks the dog, putters in the garage.

ROS: no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no palpitations he notices, no leg pain with walking, no bleeding problems on warfarin, no heartburn on the PPI. Otherwise negative.

Exam: well appearing, heavyset. Heart irregularly irregular, rate controlled, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft, nontender. Feet: skin intact, DP pulses palpable but faint bilaterally, monofilament intact. Neuro grossly nonfocal, symmetric grip, steady gait.

A/P:
1. T2DM - on metformin. A1c, UACR today. Eye exam is with an outside eye doctor yearly; will request.
2. HTN - acceptable today on lisinopril/HCTZ. CMP.
3. Permanent AF on warfarin, hx of stroke 2017 - continue metoprolol and warfarin. We will manage INRs here going forward: INR today, then about monthly, RN to call results. Keeps his yearly cardiology visit.
4. HLD - atorvastatin 40, lipids today.
5. PAD - aspirin, statin. Asked old office for any vascular studies.
6. GERD - stable on omeprazole.
7. Obesity - BMI over 30, talked about portions and walking more.
8. Former smoker, 40 pk-yr, quit 2017 - discussed annual low-dose CT screening, he is in favor. Ordered.
9. HM - Hep C and HIV screening today. Flu and shingles vaccine at a nurse visit next month. Will look for colonoscopy and tetanus dates in records.

RTC 3 months, INR monthly.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Rossi - welcome again. Your labs are back. A1c is in a good range for you, kidney function and potassium are normal, cholesterol is about where it was on your old reports. Hep C and HIV screens were negative. INR was in range, so stay on the same 5 mg dose; our nurse will call you about the next check in early October. Talk soon.

events.reason: Records from prior primary care office

reports.text: Outside study (prior primary care office records). Resting ankle-brachial index with Doppler pressures. Right ABI 0.84. Left ABI 0.79. Triphasic to biphasic waveforms at the ankles bilaterally.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from prior PCP, 61 pages, scanned to chart. Summary for the doctor:
- Hospital discharge summary 03/2017: mild ischemic stroke, full recovery, on warfarin for AF.
- ABI 04/2018: R 0.84, L 0.79 (mild PAD). Result entered.
- Colonoscopy 2018: normal, repeat in 10 years.
- Tdap 2016.
- Med list matches what he brought in. NKDA.
- No vascular imaging of the abdomen found in what they sent.

documents.title: Nurse visit - INR and vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Fingerstick INR in range today, no missed doses, no bleeding or bruising, no new meds or antibiotics. Continue warfarin 5 mg daily. Next INR in about 4-5 weeks.
Flu high-dose given L deltoid, Shingrix #1 given R deltoid. VIS reviewed. Waited 15 min, no reaction. Told him the shingles shot can make the arm sore and him tired for a day or two. Dose 2 due in 2-6 months, booked January.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
INDICATION: Annual lung cancer screening. 65-year-old former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2017. Baseline exam.
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
FINDINGS: No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear. No consolidation or effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1: negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

documents.title: INR result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with INR, in range. Same dose. Also told him the lung CT from last week was clear per Dr's note. Next INR mid December.

documents.title: Follow-up visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
3 month f/u DM, HTN, AF.

Doing fine. Taking everything. Home sugars in the morning 120s-140s. No lows. No bleeding on warfarin. No chest pain, palpitations, dyspnea, leg pain walking.

Reviewed old records: stroke 2017 fully resolved, ABI 2018 mild PAD bilaterally, colonoscopy 2018 normal, Tdap 2016.

Exam: NAD. Irregularly irregular, rate ok. Lungs clear. No edema.

A/P:
T2DM - A1c today. Same metformin.
HTN - fine, same.
AF on warfarin - INR today with the other labs, saves him a stick.
PAD - mild by ABI, asymptomatic, aspirin/statin.
LDCT 11/2019 Lung-RADS 1, repeat 1 yr.
Shingrix #2 in Jan.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Shingrix #2 R deltoid, series complete. Had a sore arm and was tired a day after the first one, nothing else. INR in range, continue 5 mg daily, recheck in a month.

documents.title: Visit converted
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt to cancel today's in-person visit per new office policy. He is fine with video. Rebooked as a video visit 4/7. Lab still open for drive-up draws, he will get his INR and A1c drawn the morning of the visit.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from home, identity confirmed, consents to video.

Staying home, getting groceries delivered. Admits more snacking and less walking the last month. Home BP cuff readings low-mid 130s/80s. Fasting sugars a bit higher, 130-150. No lows. No bleeding. Feels well.

Labs this morning: A1c 7.4, up from 7.1. Kidney function and potassium fine. INR in range.

A/P:
T2DM - A1c 7.4, higher with the lockdown. Not changing meds for this; back to walking now the weather is turning. Recheck at the fall visit.
HTN - home readings acceptable, continue.
AF/warfarin - in range, same dose. Drive-up INR monthly.
RTC fall for wellness visit.

documents.title: INR
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. Left VM with result, same dose, next draw early August. Asked him to call if he starts any antibiotic.

documents.title: Eye examination report
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Diabetic eye examination, dilated. Visual acuity 20/25 OD, 20/25 OS with correction. Anterior segments quiet. Fundus: no diabetic retinopathy either eye, maculae flat, no drusen. Impression: type 2 diabetes without retinopathy. Return one year. Copy to primary care.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV + chronic disease f/u.

Feels good. Back to walking the dog twice a day once things opened up. Weight down a kilo. Eye doctor in July: no retinopathy. No falls. Independent in all ADLs and IADLs, still drives. Hearing ok. Two-story house, bedroom upstairs, no trouble with the stairs. PHQ-2 negative. No health care proxy or advance directive yet, forms given.

No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, bleeding, claudication, heartburn.

Exam: BMI ~30. Irregularly irregular, controlled. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Feet intact, faint DP pulses as before, monofilament normal. Gait steady, gets up from the chair without using his arms.

Labs today: A1c 7.0, back down. CMP, CBC normal. LDL ~100s on atorvastatin 40. UACR normal. INR in range.

A/P:
T2DM - fine, continue metformin.
HTN - at goal today.
AF/warfarin, hx stroke - monthly INR, stable.
HLD/PAD - continue statin, aspirin.
Obesity - small loss, encouraged.
Lung screening due November, ordered.
Flu shot next month at the nurse visit. Shingrix done. Colonoscopy due 2028.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: INR low
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR 1.7, below range. Pt thinks he missed a dose or two over the holiday weekend away from home. No new meds, diet otherwise the same. Per protocol: take 7.5 mg (1.5 tabs) tonight only, then back to 5 mg daily. Recheck one week. Pt repeated back instructions.

documents.title: INR recheck
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR back in range. Continue 5 mg daily. Bought a weekly pill box. Next check in 4 weeks.

documents.title: covid vaccine
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doc, I want the covid shot as soon as we can get it. Is it ok with the warfarin? Do we sign up with you or somewhere else

documents.title: RE: covid vaccine
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Yes, you should get it and the warfarin is not a reason to wait. Hold firm pressure on the spot for a couple of minutes after the shot. For now it is going through the state sign-up and the pharmacies, not through us. You will be in an early group because of age. Send me the dates when you have them and we will put them in your chart.
